title: The look-alike sign-in link — question explanation
learningObjective: Inspect a link destination before opening it and navigate independently when uncertain
format: 16:9 educational motion-graphics video; narration; separate captions; no autoplay with sound
visualStyle: Deep navy and charcoal; restrained cyan/electric-blue highlights; limited purple accents; clean typography; purposeful, low-motion transitions; accessible contrast.

scenes.name: Scenario setup
scenes.visual: A message says you must review a shared document. The visible text says “university portal,” but the underlying link points to a misspelled domain.
scenes.direction: Show a fictional simulated setting. Use generic UI and no actual organization, brand, user identity, credential, real URL or live account.

scenes.name: Learning objective and risk cue
scenes.visual: Inspect a link destination before opening it and navigate independently when uncertain
scenes.direction: Highlight only observable cues and explain the decision context without implying certainty beyond the scenario.

scenes.name: Recommended response
scenes.visual: Option B: Do not use the link; open the known portal independently and locate the document there. Independent navigation avoids relying on a potentially deceptive destination.
scenes.direction: Animate the recommended defensive choice as a clear decision path. Display the action verb and trusted channel/control.

scenes.name: Why the other options fail
scenes.visual: Option A: Private browsing does not make a malicious destination safe. Option C: Visible link text can conceal a different destination. Option D: Search results may include look-alike or sponsored destinations and do not validate the message.
scenes.direction: Show each unsafe alternative separately with a complete, concise reason. Do not depict operational exploitation, malicious code or credential capture.

scenes.name: Defensive takeaway
scenes.visual: Use a bookmark or manually enter the service’s known address. Report the suspicious message if it is unsolicited. Treat a link’s actual destination—not its label—as the relevant address.
scenes.direction: Close with one readable takeaway and the next safe action. Keep the final frame long enough for comprehension.
scenes.onScreenText: Treat a link’s actual destination—not its label—as the relevant address.
